evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate only requires nonzero, changed manager PIDs and nonzero, changed invocation IDs. It never requires the before/after manager snapshots to share a boot ID, so a guest reboot between those observations can supply a new manager PID and invocation ID and falsely satisfy the isolated manager-restart check. Adding a nonempty equality check on the manager snapshot boot IDs closes that gap while retaining the PID/invocation checks.
